Incident VAC-AB-1-crm-practice, hypothesis V10. Session nonce: bozo-duka-lovo-pami-naju-lumi-poza-fota-jugi-hako-noni

Hypothesis: Vaccinate crm-practice with AB-1@1.0
Root cause: Retry-scoped accumulator reset: a refactor moved the progress/idempotency accumulator inside the closure that the retry wrapper re-runs, so each retry attempt rebuilds it, loses track of completed work and repeats side effects such as duplicate entries.
Approach: In sync_contacts, move the construction of the SyncSession accumulator (including any "reuse caller-supplied SyncSession or create a new one" fallback) out of the retried scope attempt and into sync_contacts's body, before the call to retry_with_backoff. That way exactly one SyncSession instance is created per call to sync_contacts and is shared by every retry attempt. attempt should only do one resumable pass driven by what SyncSession still reports as pending, and it should return that same SyncSession. Keep Which contacts of one batch are created, and where to resume., including any docstrings or renames the originating change added. Never let a retry attempt by retry_with_backoff create a new SyncSession or repeat a side effect (a write, post, or booking) that an earlier attempt already recorded in SyncSession.

content.text:
I fixed the retry bug in `sync_contacts` in `practice_crm/sync.py`, and the test suite passes (3 tests).

The `SyncSession` is now created once, in the body of `sync_contacts`, before `retry_with_backoff` is called. It uses the caller-supplied session if there is one, otherwise a new one. Previously the closure that the retry wrapper re-runs built it, so each retry started from nothing and re-created contacts that were already written.

`attempt()` now does one pass over `current.pending()` and returns that same session. Every retry resumes from the cursor and the `created` set, so a contact written before a rate limit isn't written again.

I also changed the fallback check from `session or SyncSession(batch)` to `session if session is not None else ...`. That keeps a caller-supplied session from being swapped out for a new one if it ever evaluates as falsy. `SyncSession` has no truthiness hook today, so this doesn't change current behaviour.

I haven't re-run the vaccination scenario itself (the induced 429s) — only the existing tests.
